"Mikasa Ackermann"}} is a [[Character (arts)|fictional character]] from [[Hajime Isayama]]'s [[manga]] series ''[[Attack on Titan]]''. Mikasa is introduced as a citizen of Paradis Island living with the protagonist, [[Eren Yeager]], and his family, who took her in following the deaths of her parents in an attempted kidnapping. When giant creatures known as Titans invade the area and eat Eren's mother, Mikasa and Eren become members of the Military and join the Survey Corps—an elite group of soldiers who fight Titans outside the walls, whilst studying the physiology of Titans so as to better understand and defend themselves against these creatures. Mikasa's main motivation for fighting is her love for Eren, of whom she is extremely protective. She has also appeared in video games and [[Attack on Titan (TV series)|the anime adaptation]]. Isayama based Mikasa on a real person he met before he became a manga artist, keeping the original idea of her being Asian in order to stand out within the Western look-a-like cast. Mikasa is voiced by [[Yui Ishikawa]] in the Japanese dub and [[Trina Nishimura]] in the English version of the anime. The two voice actresses were surprised by the popularity of their works and the charming aspect of Mikasa despite her usual stoicism. Mikasa's strong presence received a positive response. Being a member of the Ackermann clan, Mikasa demonstrates an outstanding skill in combat. Though she was praised for her calm personality which contrasts Eren's generally intense behavior, critics were also surprised by the softer side she shows towards Eren. Both voice actresses were also praised by the media. ==Creation and design== [[File:Memorial Ship Mikasa 211016a.jpg|thumb|left|The ''Mikasa'' battleship, which served as the inspiration for the character's first name.]] After he first moved to Tokyo, [[Hajime Isayama]] was working part time and one of his clients became the model of Mikasa. She covered her face with a scarf late at night, and the near mangaka thought this look of hers was endearing. When she came to the store, Isayama came up with the first sketch of the heroine. He was sure that the customer who became Mikasa's model was Asian, contrasting the Western-like characters often seen in the manga, most notably Eren. Only Mikasa's race as someone of Asian descent has been noted. Isayama stated that Mikasa, Levi, and Kenny are all part of the same Ackerman bloodline. However, their reasons for protecting their respective counterparts do not have anything to do with the bloodline itself—"it is just their nature."Attack on Titan ANSWERS, There are some parts of Mikasa that are "unrefined", yet on the other hand, she has a brave personality. Isayama believes he was influenced by Casca from ''[[Berserk (manga)|Berserk]]'' when writing Mikasa.{{cite book|title=Gekkan Shingeki no Kyojin|publisher=[[Kodansha]]|volume=3}} Isayama noted it was generic that a heroine is usually a woman who motivates a man, and that he did not really like that way of thinking. Although there are differences between the skeletal structure and muscle count of men and women which affects their physical strength, Isayama did not find that interesting, which is why he made Mikasa a woman who excels in combat. Isayama also claimed that he intended for Mikasa's character development to be about her separating from Eren and returning to the same girl she used to be during her childhood. Isayama said Mikasa and Armin had developed a habitual mindset of revolving around Eren and wishing to help him, and that in the future, his intention was to have the friends oppose one another. Mikasa's name is noted to come from the ''[[Japanese battleship Mikasa|Mikasa]]'', a famous [[pre-dreadnought battleship]] of the [[Imperial Japanese Navy]].{{cite web |author-link=Hajime Isayama |last=Isayama |first=Hajime |url=http://blog.livedoor.jp/isayamahazime/archives/5717708.html |script-title=ja:現在進行中の黒歴史: ネットの環境が整いましたので再開します |publisher=Blog.livedoor.jp |date=28 August 2011|access-date=5 May 2021}} Mikasa's surname is derived from the Yiddish cognate of German name "Ackermann" ("Ackerman" in Yiddish) meaning "one who works the fields."Attack on Titan Character Encyclopedia (p. 62) ===Casting=== {{multiple image | align = right | footer = Yui Ishikawa (''left'') and Trina Nishimura voice Mikasa in Japanese and English, respectively. | image1 = Jurassic World Fallen Kingdom Japan Premiere Red Carpet Ishikawa Yui (43101892301).jpg | width1 = 130 | alt1 = | image2 =Trina Nishimura by Gage Skidmore.jpg | width2 = 150 | alt2 = }} Mikasa is voiced by [[Yui Ishikawa]] in Japanese,{{Ref label|GB|GB p.20}} and by [[Trina Nishimura]] in the English dub.{{cite web |url=http://www.funimation.com/blog/2014/03/13/attack-on-titan-cast-announcement-day-4 |title=Attack on Titan Cast Announcement – Day 4 |work=[[Funimation]] |date=14 March 2014|last=Lee |first=Michelle|access-date=13 March 2023}}{{cite web|last=Loo|first=Egan|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2014-03-14/funimation-announces-5th-round-of-attack-on-titan-dub-cast |title=Funimation Announces 5th Round of Attack on Titan Dub Cast |work=[[Anime News Network]] |date=14 March 2014|access-date=13 March 2023}} Ishikawa said that Mikasa cares mainly about Eren, and remains generally aloof from the rest of the world. She says that "While she might seem like a character with so few emotional levels, there are actually many feelings that swirl around her heart."{{Ref label|GB|GB p.20}} She did not read the original work until being told about the audition for the anime. Upon reading the ''Attack on Titan'' manga, Ishikawa was attracted by the mystery and development of the character. Ishikawa wanted the role for the series and was surprised by the popularity she obtained across the years.{{cite web|last=Bertschy|first=Zac|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/feature/2017-07-24/interview-attack-on-titan-trina-nishimura-and-yui-ishikawa/.119152|title=Interview: Attack on Titan's Trina Nishimura and Yui Ishikawa|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=24 July 2017|access-date=10 March 2023}} Trina Nishimura learned of the series from her brother, who showed her the first episode of the anime. She was immediately impressed by it. Nishimura expressed pressure when auditioning for the role and was surprised by the large popularity it had. She often listened to recordings of Ishikawa's work to get experience about the portrayal of Mikasa. While recording the series, she avoided reading the manga because it could ruin her work. Like Ishikawa, Nishimura enjoyed Mikasa's love confession for being able to provide comfort to Eren in the middle of a dark scene. Meanwhile, Nishimura often talked with voice actor director [[Mike McFarland]] in regards to her work as she had poor views on her own work. With the coming of the final story arc in the anime adaptation, Nishimura was committed to the new developments of her character, especially in her reintroduction. She befriended Eren's English actor [[Bryce Papenbrook]]. During recordings of the final season, Nishimura commented that while Mikasa is not well known for emoting, she notably became sad more often—which Nishimura saw as a major improvement over her earlier characterisation. She suggested that Mikasa should be made to choose between her devotion to the Military and her love for Eren as a result of major developments in the story, but did not want to expand on that. The increasing violence of the series led to Nishimura's fear of Mikasa being killed every time she had to do recording of the series.{{cite web|last=Lukas|first=Alex|url=https://www.cbr.com/attack-on-titan-interview-mikasa-hange-voice-actors/|title=Attack on Titan Interview: Mikasa & Hange's Voice Actors on Season 4 Hopes & Fears|website=[[Comic Book Resources]]|date=7 December 2020|access-date=10 March 2023}} In the [[live-action]] film, she is portrayed by [[Kiko Mizuhara]].{{cite web |url=https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/attack-titan-shingeki-no-kyojin-movie-cast-photos/ |title=Live-action 'Attack on Titan' cast photos revealed |access-date=5 May 2021|date=20 November 2014 |website=The Daily Dot}} Mizuhara referred to Mikasa as an inspiring character due to her strength as well as caring due to the love she shows towards Eren.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HWGBtaXbDSs|title=ATTACK ON TITAN Live Action Movie Actor & Director Interviews Kiko Mizuhara, Haruma Miura|work=That Hashtag Show|date=29 September 2015 |access-date=11 March 2023}} ==Appearances== ===In ''Attack on Titan''=== Mikasa is Eren's childhood friend taken in by his family after seeing her parents brutally murdered by human traffickers. She is shown to feel gratitude toward them as caretakers, as well as Eren, who had saved her life and given her an iconic scarf. Before living with the Yeager family, Mikasa had appeared to be a cheerful, outgoing, and gentle child; but her parents' tragic deaths had an overwhelming influence on her, causing her to lose her innocence and realise the world's cruelty. This caused her to become quieter and more withdrawn, maintaining a stoic expression except when it comes to Eren and her friends.{{Ref label|GB|GB p. 36}} As Eren's committed caretaker, she feels compelled to follow and protect him at all costs, even joining him in the Survey Corps. Graduating from the Training Corps at the top of her class,{{gnr|ch|2}} she is regarded by officers as an unprecedented genius and prodigy, easily worth a hundred soldiers in battle.{{gnr|vol|3|, |4}} As later revealed, this is due to Mikasa's father being a descendant of the Ackerman clan, an Eldian bloodline that was genetically modified to create super soldiers equal to a Titan in strength, originally designed to protect Eldia's king. When under duress, these genetically inherited abilities may allow a descendant access to their ancestors' battle experience. Mikasa's Ackerman instincts were first awakened in the aftermath of her parents' deaths when Eren urged her to 'fight' back against her kidnappers.{{gnr|ch|6}}{{ref label|ep 6|ep 6|3}} Though technically half-blooded, she is also the last known person of Asian descent residing in the Walls. A wrist tattoo of the Azumabito crest inherited from her mother indicates that she is descended from the prominent {{nihongo|Azumabito family|アズマビト家|Azumabito-ke}}, a cadet Shogun branch from the Oriental nation of {{nihongo|Hizuru|ヒィズル|Hizuru}}, whose ancestors migrated from their native land to Paradis as honored ambassadors.{{gnr|ch|6}}{{ref label|ep 6|ep 6|2}}{{Ref label|GB|GB p.39}} While investigating Marley's volunteer soldiers with the Survey Corps, Eren reveals to Mikasa that he has always hated being "forced" to become Ackerman's blood slave and protect Eren. In turn, she becomes despondent and removes her scarf from her neck. While still caring for Eren, Mikasa decides to join the alliance to stop Eren's planned genocide on the world. In the climax against Eren's forces, Mikasa experienced a Paths dream of an alternate scenario where she and Eren escaped from the military and are living together. Eren asks her to forget about him upon his death before Mikasa recovers. She puts the scarf back on, deciding she will not fulfill his request and kills him, placing a kiss on his lips, asserting she would see him later. In the aftermath, Eren confesses to Armin that he had actually loved Mikasa and cared for his allies but did not want to drag them into his massacre. Mikasa buries Eren underneath a tree on a hill near Shiganshina District, continuing to visit his grave as she spends the rest of her life in peace, passing on as an old woman while still wearing the scarf Eren gave her. Overall, Mikasa has gorgeous black hair, dazzling grey eyes. Mikasa has a scar in her right cheek, given by Eren mistakenly during his Titan form. She wears the survey corps uniform along with a red scarf, given by her lover. ===In other media=== Mikasa features in multiple [[video game]]s associated with the ''[[Attack on Titan]]'' series, including: ''[[Attack on Titan (video game)|Attack on Titan]]'', ''[[Attack on Titan 2]]'', ''Valkyrie Connect'', ''[[Granblue Fantasy]]'', ''[[Disgaea RPG]]'', ''The Alchemist Code'', ''[[Attack on Titan: Humanity in Chains|Humanity in Chains]]'', ''[[Star Ocean: Anamnesis]]'', and many others.{{Cite web |title=Mikasa Ackerman Games |url=https://www.giantbomb.com/mikasa-ackerman/3005-28032/games/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Giant Bomb |language=en}} Mikasa also features as an in-game cosmetic in the massive [[battle royale game]], ''[[Fortnite]]''. They are a crew formed by the strongest fighters of the Kuja, including Hancok's two younger sisters who possess the Zoan-type abilities of the {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit|ヘビヘビの実|Hebi Hebi no Mi}} branch.{{gnr|ch|519}} The Boa sisters are known as the "Gorgon Sisters", being based on the three [[Gorgons]] of the [[Greek mythology]], while the members of the crew are based on the [[Amazons]].{{cite web |url=https://www.animeherald.com/2024/01/13/one-piece-keeps-greek-mythology-alive-with-boa-hancock/ |title=One Piece Keeps Greek Mythology Alive With Boa Hancock |author= Caitlin Sinclair Chappell |date=January 13, 2024 |website=Anime Herald}} ====Boa Hancock==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Hancock'''|ボア・ハンコック|Boa Hankokku}} is a member of the all-female [[Kuja Tribe]] from the island of Amazon Lily.{{gnr|ch|515|f.}} Sold to the [[World Government (One Piece)#Celestial Dragons|Celestial Dragons]] during childhood, she and her sisters are force-fed devil fruits and [[Human branding|branded]] as slaves.{{gnr|ch|521}} Eventually freed by [[#Fisher Tiger|Fisher Tiger]], the three return to their people. Hancock becomes ruler and is referred to by her subjects as {{nihongo|"'''Snake Princess'''"|蛇姫|Hebihime}}.{{gnr|ch|516|, |521}} Leading the Kuja Pirates, she quickly gains infamy as the {{nihongo|"'''Pirate Empress'''"|海賊女帝|Kaizoku Jotei}} and is offered membership in the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|516|, |522}} Despite resenting the World Government for her past enslavement, which she keeps a secret even from her kinswomen, Hancock accepts the position to protect her people. But when called upon to participate in the Government's war against the [[Whitebeard Pirates]], she initially refuses and only reconsiders after falling in love with [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]], who enlists her help to infiltrate [[Impel Down]].{{gnr|ch|516|f., |520|–|522}} The ability of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Love-Love Fruit|メロメロの実|Mero Mero no Mi}} allows her to turn anyone charmed by her into stone and back again, with the sole exception of Luffy due to his lack of any sexual interest in her.{{gnr|ch|516|, |521}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/strong-female-devil-fruit-users/ |title=15 Strongest Female Devil Fruit Users In One Piece |author=Kara Ketchum |date=June 21, 2023|website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} Her fruit's abilities can also be countered by forcing yourself to feel another emotion that drowns out your lust, for example pain, as shown when Vice Admiral Momonga avoided being turned to stone by stabbing himself in the hand. She is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. After the most recent Reverie, the Seven Warlords were disbanded, making her an enemy of the World Government again. In the Japanese anime television series, her voice actress is [[Kotono Mitsuishi]].{{cite video |year=2011 |title=One Piece: 12thシーズン 女ヶ島篇: Piece.01 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} In the Funimation English adaptation, her voice is supplied by [[Lydia Mackay]]. Her abilities are based on those of the Gorgon [[Medusa]] in [[Greek mythology]]. =====Salome===== {{nihongo|'''Salome'''|サロメ|Sarome}} is Boa Hancock's pet snake who supports her in battle, and also acts as her throne that she sits on. He is white with patches of red. He wears a skull upon his head. ====Boa Sandersonia==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Sandersonia'''|ボア・サンダーソニア|Boa Sandāsonia}} is the middle sister whose {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit: Model Anaconda|ヘビヘビの実 モデル アナコンダ|Hebi Hebi no Mi: Moderu Anakonda}} enables her to transform into an [[anaconda]] or anaconda-human hybrid. Boa Sandersonia is voiced by [[Chiwa Saitō]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Lindsay Seidel]] in the Funimation dub. ====Boa Marigold==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Marigold'''|ボア・マリーゴールド|Boa Marīgōrudo}} is the youngest sister whose {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit: Model King Cobra|ヘビヘビの実 モデル キングコブラ|Hebi Hebi no Mi: Moderu Kingu Kobura}} enables her to turn into a [[king cobra]] or king cobra-human hybrid. Boa Marigold is voiced by [[Kimiko Saitō]] in the original Japanese version and by Julie Mayfield in the Funimation dub. ===={{visible anchor|Shakky|Shakuyaku}}==== {{nihongo|'''Shakuyaku'''|シャクヤク}}, most commonly known by her nickname "'''Shakky'''", was the Empress and captain of the Kuja Pirates after Gloriosa. Her extreme popularity in comparison to Gloriosa led to her eventually taking over the post, but nevertheless retires to open a bar on Fullalead.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1156|,|1158}} Her kidnapping by the World Government led to the God Valley Incident.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1159}} Both the [[#Rocks Pirates|Rocks Pirates]] and the [[#Roger Pirates|Roger Pirates]] arrived where they each wanted to rescue her.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1160}} After the Roger Pirates disband, she marries [[#Silvers Rayleigh|Silvers Rayleigh]] and works as a bartender at Sabaody Archipelago. Shakuyaku is voiced by [[Hiromi Tsuru]] in the original Japanese version, [[Masumi Asano]] in Episode 870 of the original Japanese version, and by [[Elizabeth Maxwell]] in the Funimation dub. ====Gloriosa==== {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Gloriosa}}'''|グロリオーサ|Guroriōsa}}, more commonly referred to as "'''Elder Nyon'''", is a short elderly woman who was the Empress of Amazon Lily and the captain of the Kuja Pirates approximately 60 years before current events. She also was a member of the [[#Rocks Pirates|Rocks Pirates]]. She fell in love with [[Gol D. Roger]], only to leave behind her post and subsequently the country after his rejection in favor of Shakuyaku.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1156}} Gloriosa is voiced by [[Ako Mayama]] in the original Japanese version and by Nancy Sherrand in the Funimation dub. ====Other Kuja pirates==== * {{nihongo|'''Marguerite'''|マーガレット|Māgaretto}}: A warrior who befriends Luffy. {{nihongo||[[wikt:蝙蝠|蝙蝠]]|kōmori}}}} is the captain of the island-sized ship ''Thriller Bark'', leader of Thriller Bark's Mysterious Four, and a former member of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|448}} The {{nihongo|Shadow-Shadow Fruit|カゲカゲの実|Kage Kage no Mi}} grants him the ability to control his shadow, allowing it to act completely independent from his body, and to control others' shadows.{{gnr|ch|455|, |463}} After his entire crew that made up the Gecko Pirates is annihilated by [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], he creates a completely obedient, immortal army of zombies by {{nihongo|'''Perona'''|ペローナ|Perōna}}, also known as {{nihongo|"'''Ghost Princess'''"|ゴーストプリンセス|Gōsuto Purinsesu}}, is a member of the Thriller Bark Pirates and member of Thriller Bark's Mysterious Four. She is a woman dressed in a [[Gothic Lolita]]-style who can create ghosts with various abilities thanks to the power of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Hollow-Hollow Fruit|ホロホロの実|Horo Horo no Mi}}.{{gnr|ch|443|, |461}} After [[#Gecko Moria|Gecko Moria]]'s defeat, Perona takes shelter in [[Dracule Mihawk]]'s castle, where she begrudgingly helps and cooperates with [[Roronoa Zoro]] in his training during the timeskip.{{gnr|ch|597}} Perona later separates from Mihawk and travels to Hachinosu after finding out that Gecko is still alive.{{gnr|ch|1080}} In the original Japanese anime series, Perona is voiced by [[Kumiko Nishihara]]. In the Funimation English adaptation, her voice actress is [[Felecia Angelle]]. ====Hogback==== {{nihongo|'''Hogback'''|ホグバック|Hogubakku}} was a world-famous doctor and is Moria's medical servant and member of Thriller Bark's Mysterious Four, who was given [[unlife]] in the form of shadows stolen using Moria's Devil Fruit ability.{{gnr|ch|446|, |449|, |455}} Hogback is voiced by [[Hiroshi Iwasaki]] in the original Japanese version and by Marcus D. Stimac in the Funimation dub. ====Absalom==== "Graveyard" {{nihongo|'''Absalom'''|アブサロム|Abusaromu}} is a patchwork man and member of Thriller Bark's Mysterious Four augmented by Hogback with the snout of a lion, the skin of an elephant, and the muscles of a bear and a gorilla. He can turn himself and anything he touches invisible thanks to the Clear-Clear Fruit. Absalom later became a freelance writer and leaked information about an alliance between the Hawkins Pirates, the Kid Pirates, and the On Air Pirates.{{gnr|ch|700}} Absalom is captured by the [[Blackbeard Pirates]], brought to Hachinosu, and killed by [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Shiryu|Shiryu]], who steals his Devil Fruit power.{{gnr|ch|925}} Absalom is voiced by [[Hiroaki Miura]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Andrew Chandler (actor)|Andrew Chandler]] in the Funimation dub. ====Wild Zombies==== {{nihongo|'''Wild Zombies'''|動物ゾンビ|Wairudo Zonbi}} are zombies commanded by Perona. Oars is voiced by [[Mayumi Tanaka]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Colleen Clinkenbeard]] in the Funimation dub. ===Sun Pirates=== {{see also|Jimbei|#Fisher Tiger}} [[File:Sun Pirates Jolly Roger.svg|thumb|200px|The Sun Pirates' Jolly Roger, an alteration of the Hoof of the Soaring Dragon.]] The {{nihongo|'''Sun Pirates'''|タイヨウの海賊団|Taiyō no Kaizokudan}} are a band of pirates consisting of fish-men and [[Merman|mermen]] that was originally led by [[#Fisher Tiger|Fisher Tiger]] and later by [[Jimbei]]. They attack any pirate ship they see, but no matter who is on it, they never kill directly.{{gnr|ch|622}} Their Sun insignia was created to cover up the mark of the Celestial Dragon's slave, "Hoof of the Soaring Dragon", since many on the crew bore the mark from being enslaved. The Sun insignia was designed to completely cover the Hoof branding, so the World Government was unable to know which crew member to kidnap and re-enslave due confusion over their former status.{{gnr|ch|620}} The members of the [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]] and [[#Macro Pirates|Macro Pirates]] were also members of the crew.{{gnr|ch|622}} The Sun Pirates temporarily shelter a human child, [[Koala (One Piece)|Koala]], who escaped from Marijoa during Tiger's liberation,{{gnr|ch|622}} and eventually return her to her parents on Foolshout Island, where a Marine ambush led by Rear Admiral Strawberry results in Tiger's death.{{gnr|ch|623}} With Arlong imprisoned, Jimbei took over the Sun Pirates until he joined the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]]; as part of Jimbei's conditions for accepting the role, which he believes will bring Queen Otohime's dream closer to reality, Arlong is released, but he and the rest of the Arlong Pirates leave the crew, as well as the members of the Macro Pirates.{{gnr|ch|624}} The Sun Pirates later served under Big Mom as her subordinates, until Jinbe decided to abandon their alliance with her. They helped the Straw Hats escape from Big Mom's territory.{{cite web|url=http://books.shueisha.co.jp/CGI/search/syousai_put.cgi?isbn_cd=978-4-08-881496-4|title=One Piece/89|publisher=Shueisha|access-date=May 17, 2018|language=ja|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523205807/http://books.shueisha.co.jp/CGI/search/syousai_put.cgi?isbn_cd=978-4-08-881496-4|archive-date=May 23, 2018|url-status=live}}{{cite book|title=One Piece/89|publisher=Viz Media|isbn=1974705218}} The current known members of the Sun Pirates are: * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Aladine}}'''|アラディン|Aradin}}: A [[Brotula multibarbata|goatsbeard brotula]]-type merman who is the crew's doctor and first mate during Jimbei's leadership. Aladine was once enslaved and is now married to Charlotte Praline. Aladine is voiced by [[Takashi Nagasako]] in the original Japanese version and by Brad Smeaton in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Charlotte Praline}}'''|シャーロット・プラリネ|Shārotto Purarine}}: Aladine's wife and [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]]'s 21st daughter who is a hybrid of a human and a hammerhead shark-type merman. She is the younger twin sister of [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Charlotte Prim|Charlotte Prim]]. Charlotte Praline is voiced by Yuko Tachibana in the original Japanese version and by Sara Ragsdale in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Wadatsumi}}'''|ワダツミ}}: A giant [[Takifugu rubripes|tiger blowfish]]-type fish-man who is a former member of the [[#New Fish-Man–Flying Pirates Alliance|Flying Pirates]].  (Arms‑Arms)}} |- | colspan=5 style="background:#daf;font-size:10%;" |   |- ! rowspan=2 | Other Officers ! colspan=2 | Monet ! colspan=2 | [[#Donquixote Rosinante|Donquixote Rosinante (Corazon)]] |- | colspan=2 | (Snow-Snow) | colspan=2 | (Calm-Calm) |} The {{nihongo|'''Donquixote Family'''|ドンキホーテファミリー|Donkihōte Famirī}}, also called the {{nihongo|'''Donquixote Pirates'''|ドンキホーテ海賊団|Donkihōte Kaizoku-dan}}, are a powerful crew led by [[#Donquixote Doflamingo|Donquixote Doflamingo]].{{gnr|ch|762}} The figurative family is split into three divisions, each led by one of the top three officers: the [[#Trébol Army|Trébol Army]], [[#Diamante Army|Diamante Army]] and [[#Pica Army|Pica Army]].{{gnr|ch|732}} [[Bellamy (One Piece)|Bellamy]] and [[List of One Piece characters#Kyuin|Kyuin]] were members of the crew, and [[Caesar Clown]] and [[List of One Piece characters#Disco|Disco]] were also their subordinates. ====Donquixote Doflamingo==== {{nihongo|'''Donquixote Doflamingo'''|ドンキホーテ・ドフラミンゴ|Donkihōte Dofuramingo}} is the captain of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], the usurper king of the island Dressrosa, and formerly one of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|234|, |682|, |728}} The {{nihongo|String-String Fruit|イトイトの実|Ito Ito no Mi}} grants him the ability to control others using movements with his fingers resembling a [[puppeteer]]'s. It also enables him to control sharp thin strings from his fingertips that can cut people, create clones of himself, and attach to the clouds in the sky to allow him to fly.{{gnr|ch|231}} He is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. He is also a former Celestial Dragon after his father, Donquixote Homing, decided to abandon that life to become a normal human. However, they were chased by the people, tortured, and eventually Doflamingo killed his father. He brought the head of his father back to Mariejois in hopes of receiving his Celestial title back again. He was denied and later became a pirate. He believes that the "Great Pirate Era" is nearing its end and a new age is about to begin.{{gnr|ch|303}} He is a [[broker]] under the alias of "{{visible anchor|Joker}}", and owns a large auction house at the Sabaody Archipelago, where humans and other species are sold as slaves.{{gnr|ch|504}} Eventually after the Straw Hat Crew and Dressrosa's citizens reveal his treacherous deeds, Doflamingo is defeated by Luffy and his title is revoked leading to the arrest of him and his pirate crew. He is voiced by [[Hideyuki Tanaka]].{{cite video |year=2004 |title=6thシーズン 空島·スカイピア篇: Piece.03 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} In the Funimation English adaptation, his voice is supplied by [[Robert McCollum]].{{cite video |year=2010 |title=One Piece: Season 3: First Voyage |medium=DVD |publisher=Funimation Entertainment |isbn=978-1-4210-2119-5 }} ====Elite Officers==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Trébol}}'''|トレーボル|Torēboru}}: The leader of the [[#Trébol Army|Trébol Army]], occupying the Club seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], with the powers of the Stick-Stick Fruit (ベタベタの実, Beta Beta no Mi) which allows him to generate an adhesive and highly sticky liquid. Trébol is voiced by [[Taiki Matsuno]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Alejandro Saab]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Diamante}}'''|ディアマンテ}}: The leader of the [[#Diamante Army|Diamante Army]], occupying the Diamond seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], who has the powers of the Ripple-Ripple Fruit (ヒラヒラの実, Hira Hira no Mi) which allows him to flatten, reform, and fold anything while still retaining its original characteristics. Diamante is voiced by [[Hideyuki Umezu]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Brad Hawkins (actor)|Brad Hawkins]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Pica}}'''|ピーカ|Pīka}}: The leader of the [[#Pica Army|Pica Army]], occupying the Spade seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], and a large, muscular man with a comically high voice with the powers of the Stone-Stone Fruit (イシイシの実, Ishi Ishi no Mi), which allows him to absorb, manipulate, and merge with stone. Pica is voiced by [[Yūji Mitsuya]] in the original Japanese version and by Ry McKeand in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Vergo}}'''|ヴェルゴ|Berugo}}: A tall, light-skinned, lean, yet muscular man who is an elite officer of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], formerly occupying the Heart seat and went by the code name "Corazon" before [[#Donquixote Rosinante|Rosinante]], undercover as a [[Marines (One Piece)|Naval vice admiral]] heading G-5 in Punk Hazard. He is a practitioner of Rokushiki and is also proficient in the use of Armament Haki. After being defeated by [[#Trafalgar Law|Law]], he dies when the SAD Production Room explodes he was in. Vergo is voiced by [[Junichi Suwabe]] in the original Japanese version and by Wes Frazierin the Funimation dub. ====Donquixote Pirates' Officers==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Trébol Army}}'''|トレーボル軍|Torēboru-gun}} is a division of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]] led by [[#Trébol|Trébol]] specializing in missions that require users with special powers.{{gnr|ch|732}} Its officers consists of: ** {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Sugar}}'''|シュガー|Shugā}}: A girl ranked as a "special officer" of the Trébol Army with the powers of the Hobby-Hobby Fruit (ホビホビの実, Hobi Hobi no Mi), which allows her to turn people into [[toy]]s. Her fruit also makes her retain the appearance of a little girl, without aging. Sugar is voiced by [[Rie Kugimiya]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Natalie Hoover]] in the Funimation. ** {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Giolla}}'''|ジョーラ|Jōra}}: A woman with the powers of the Art-Art Fruit (アトアトの実, Ato Ato no Mi) which allows her to transform things into [[modern art]]. Giolla is voiced by [[Hiroko Emori]] in the original Japanese version and by CJ Critt in the Funimation dub. ** '''[[List of One Piece characters#Viola|Viola]]''', under the code name {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Violet}}'''|ヴィオラ|Baioretto}}, was also part of the Trébol Army. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Diamante Army}}'''|ディアマンテ軍|Diamante-gun}}: A division of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]] led by [[#Diamante|Diamante]] specializing in fighting missions.{{gnr|ch|732}} Its officers consists of: ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Lao G}}'''|ラオ・G|Rao Jī}}: An old skilled martial artist obsessed with the letter G. Lao G is voiced by [[Tetsuo Gotō]] in the original Japanese version and by Jim White in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Machvise}}'''|マッハバイス|Mahhabaisu}}: A strong man with the powers of the Ton-Ton Fruit (トントンの実, Ton Ton no Mi) which allows him to change his weight at will. Machvise is voiced by [[Naomi Kusumi]] in the original Japanese version and by Shawn Gann in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Senor Pink}}'''|セニョール・ピンク|Senyōru Pinku}}: A "hard boiled" man with the power of the Swim-Swim Fruit (スイスイの実, Sui Sui no Mi) which allows him to swim through the ground or walls. Senor Pink is voiced by [[Kazuhiro Yamaji]] in the original Japanese version and by Ethan Gallardo in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Dellinger}}'''|デリンジャー|Derinjā}}: A boy who is a hybrid of a human and a [[Siamese fighting fish]]-type fishman. He primarily fights with kicks. Dellinger is voiced by [[Kōki Miyata]] in the original Japanese version and by Brandon McInnes in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Pica Army}}'''|ピーカ軍|Pīka-gun}} is a division of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]] led by [[#Pica|Pica]] specializing in commando missions.{{gnr|ch|732}} Its officers consists of: ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Buffalo}}'''|バッファロー|Baffarō}}: An extremely large man with the powers of the Spin-Spin Fruit (グルグルの実, Guru Guru no Mi) which allows him to rotate any part of his body like a [[propeller]]. Buffalo is voiced by [[Yasuhiro Takato]] in the original Japanese version and by Travis Mullenix in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Gladius}}'''|グラディウス|Guradiusu}}: A man with the powers of the Pop-Pop Fruit (パムパムの実, Pamu Pamu no Mi) which allows him to make his own body or any inorganic object he touches rupture and explode. Gladius is voiced by [[Isshin Chiba]] in the original Japanese version and by Taylor Harris in the Funimation dub. ** '''[[Straw Hats#Baby 5|Baby 5]]''' was also part of the Pica Army. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Monet}}'''|モネ|Mone}}: A [[harpy]]-like woman, officer of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]],{{gnr|ch|732}} and [[Caesar Clown]]'s lab assistant with the ability to generate, control, or transform into [[snow]] thanks to the powers of the Snow-Snow Fruit. Her bird parts were the replacements for her original parts. Monet was killed when Caesar accidentally stabbed her removed heart instead of Smoker's removed heart. Monet is voiced by [[Naoko Matsui]] in the original Japanese version and by Janelle Lutz in the Funimation dub. ===Hanafuda=== "King of Lizards" {{nihongo|'''Hanafuda'''|ハナフダ}} was a former Warlord of the Sea. He is the father of [[Ulti (One Piece)|Ulti]] and [[Page One (One Piece)|Page One]] and entrusted them to [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] after agreeing to serve the Animal Kingdom Pirates. He used to collect Ancient Zoan Devil Fruits. After he was defeated by [[Portgas D. Ace]], Hanafuda was stripped of his title and replaced by Bartholomew Kuma. He was later killed by a rival pirate. Doflamingo replaced Hanafuda's relationship with the Animal Kingdom Pirates.{{gnr|vol|111|:SBS}} ===Bartholomew Kuma=== The {{nihongo|"'''Tyrant'''"|暴君|Bōkun}} {{nihongo|'''Bartholomew Kuma'''|バーソロミュー・くま|Bāsoromyū Kuma|{{nihongo||[[wikt:熊|熊]]|kuma}} meaning [[bear]]}}, is one of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]]; the only one with a reputation for complete obedience to the World Government, when in fact he is an officer of the [[List of One Piece characters#Revolutionary Army|Revolutionary Army]].{{gnr|ch|234|, |473|f., |603}} He was formerly a slave with Emporio Ivankov and Ginny, saving others at the God Valley incident before escaping. He later became the King of the Sorbet Kingdom, raising Jewelry Bonney, Ginny's daughter, from childhood.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1098}} The power of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Paw-Paw Fruit|ニキュニキュの実|Nikyu Nikyu no Mi}} allows his palms to repel anything, from physical objects such as people or air to abstracts such as pain and fatigue.{{gnr|ch|484|f.}} He can use this ability to safely transport himself or others over long distances.{{gnr|ch|514}} Kuma is the model for the {{anchor|Pacifista}}{{nihongo|Pacifista|パシフィスタ|Pashifisuta}}, a class of experimental cyborgs created by Dr. Vegapunk for the Government. Their bodies are made of a substance harder than steel, and they can shoot powerful blasts from their mouths that can melt metal.{{gnr|ch|485}} The other Pacifista look just like Kuma, sharing his towering, bear-like stature, but lack the Paw-Paw Fruit's ability. Instead, they are able to shoot laser beams based on Admiral Kizaru's Glint-Glint Fruit laser abilities from their palms.{{gnr|ch|508|f.}} At some point during his gradual conversion into the human weapon {{anchor|PX-0}}"PX-0", Kuma's personality is erased, leaving him a programmable fighting machine under the Government's control until becoming a slave-to-rent for the World Nobles as punishment for aiding Luffy.{{gnr|ch|559|f.}} However, parts of his personality gradually returned as he unexpectedly ran across the Grand Line to Egghead to save Bonney, enough to recognize her and attack Jaygarcia Saturn; he became a companion of the Straw Hat Crew on their escape, arriving on Elbaph with them. Teach|Blackbeard]], eventually became known as the {{nihongo|"'''Worst Generation'''"|最悪の世代|Saiaku no Sedai}} by the World Government as they gained more notoriety for their crimes and, sometimes, their willingness to challenge the [[status quo]].{{gnr|ch|664}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-worst-generation-bounty-ranked/ |title=One Piece: Every Worst Generation Member's Bounty, Ranked From Lowest to Highest |author=Rylie Clothier |date=August 2, 2025 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} ===Basil Hawkins=== {{nihongo|'''Basil Hawkins'''|バジル・ホーキンス|Bajiru Hōkinsu}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Magician'''"|魔術師|Majutsushi}}, is the captain of the {{visible anchor|Hawkins Pirates}}, originating from the North Blue. He ate the {{nihongo|Straw-Straw Fruit|ワラワラの実|Wara Wara no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to create and manipulate straw. He can cover himself in straw and make [[scarecrow]]-like straw avatars to aid his offense.{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/unique-one-piece-devil-fruits/ |title=What Are The Most Unique Devil Fruit Powers in One Piece? |author=Christian Markle |date=August 9, 2023 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} He also has a habit of reading tarot cards to find out what is going to happen and the percentage probability that what he predicts will happen. After the two year timeskip, he tried to form an alliance with [[#Scratchmen Apoo|Scratchmen Apoo]] and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]. After [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] appeared in front of them, he ended up joining the [[Animal Kingdom Pirates]] as Kaido's subordinate, betraying Kid along with Apoo, and becoming one of the crew's Headliners. During the battle on Onigashima, he ended up facing [[#Killer|Killer]], ultimately being defeated by him. Basil Hawkins is voiced by [[Shigenori Sōya]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Taliesin Jaffe]] in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life buccaneer [[Basil Ringrose]] and the privateer [[John Hawkins (naval commander)|John Hawkins]].{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-characters-based-on-real-people/ |title=One Piece Characters Based On Historical Figures |date=October 24, 2024 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} ===Capone Bege=== {{nihongo|'''Capone''' "'''Gang'''" '''Bege'''|カポネ・“ギャング”・ベッジ|Kapone "Gyangu" Bejji}} is a [[Crime boss|mafia don]] turned pirate. He has the power of the {{nihongo|Castle-Castle Fruit|シロシロの実|Shiro Shiro no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to create and maintain a dimensional fortress inside his body, being able to put people inside after being reduced when approaching the entrances of his body, or transforming into a great castle that serves as a fortress.{{gnr|ch|812}} During the two year time skip, Bege became one of the [[Big Mom Pirates]]' combatants until he formed an alliance with Luffy and [[Caesar Clown]] to finish off Big Mom. Bege is married to [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]] and they are both the parents of {{nihongo|Capone Pez|カポネ・ペッツ|Kapone Pettsu}}. Capone Bege is voiced by [[Naoki Tatsuta]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Kyle Hebert]] in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life gangster [[Al Capone]]. ===={{visible anchor|Fire Tank Pirates|Firetank Pirates}}==== The {{nihongo|'''Fire Tank Pirates'''|ファイアタンク海賊団|Faia Tanku Kaizokudan}} are Capone Bege's pirate crew, originating from the West Blue. Later on, they incorporate the Rolling Pirates into their crew. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Vito}}'''|ヴィト}}: Nicknamed {{nihongo|"Phantom Gun"|怪銃|Kaijū|{{lit}} "Monster Gun"}}, is Bege's advisor.{{gnr|ch|813}} Vito is voiced by [[Daisuke Kishio]] in the original Japanese version and by Chris Hackney in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Gotti}}'''|ゴッティ}}: Bege's combatant.{{gnr|ch|825}} He is married to [[#Charlotte Lola|Charlotte Lola]] of the Rolling Pirates.{{gnr|ch|993}} Gotti is voiced by [[Masafumi Kimura]] in the original Japanese version and by Joshua Passmore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Charlotte Chiffon}}'''|シャーロット・シフォン|Shārotto Shifon}}: Is Bege's wife, and they are both the parents of Capone Pez. She is [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]]'s 22nd daughter, as well as [[#Pound|Pound]]'s daughter, and Charlotte Lola's twin sister. Chiffon is voiced by [[Aya Hisakawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Kate Bristol]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Charlotte Lola}}'''|シャーロット•ローラ|Shārotto Rōra}}: Captain of the Rolling Pirates. She and her crew were among the victims of [[#Gecko Moria|Gecko Moria]] in Thriller Bark. She is the 23rd daughter of [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]] and twin sister of [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]]. Lola ran away from Totto Land when her mother wanted her to marry [[Loki (One Piece)|Prince Loki]] of Elbaph, deciding to sail in the sea to find someone she truly loved. During her trip, she asked all the men she met if they wanted to marry her, eventually marrying [[#Gotti|Gotti]] in a merging of the Fire Tank Pirates and the Rolling Pirates.{{gnr|ch|993}} Lola is voiced by [[Aya Hisakawa]] in the original Japanese version and by Alex Moore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Risky Brothers}}'''|リスキー兄弟|Risukī Kyōdai}}: Two Rolling Pirates crew members who keep track of all the times their Lola has been rejected by the men. The tallest of the duo is voiced by Yūsuke Numata in the original Japanese version and by Brandon Jerome Bristowe in the Funimation dub, while the shortest of the duo is voiced by Tamotsu Nishiwaki in the original Japanese version and by Ian Moore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Pound}}'''|パウンド|Paundo}}: A 24 ft. human who is the 25th ex-husband of Big Mom and the father of [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]] and [[#Charlotte Lola|Charlotte Lola]]. After he was discarded by Big Mom, Pound worked to reunite with his daughters which led to his encounter with the Straw Hat Crew. Though he got burned rescuing Chiffon's group from [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Charlotte Oven|Charlotte Oven]],{{gnr|ch|887}} he was later found adrift by the [[Tontatta Pirates]] and was taken to Dressrosa to be healed.{{gnr|ch|979}} Pound later proved to Chiffon and Lola that he was their father when he saved their ship from an attack by a Marine ship.{{gnr|ch|989}} The Fire Tank Pirates pulled him aboard. Pound later attended the wedding of Lola and [[#Gotti|Gotti]].{{gnr|ch|993}} Pound is voiced by [[Masami Kikuchi]] in the original Japanese version and by Patrick McAllister in the Funimation dub. ===Jewelry Bonney=== {{nihongo|'''Jewelry Bonney'''|ジュエリー・ボニー|Juerī Bonī}} is one of twelve pirates collectively known as the [[#Worst Generation|Worst Generation]] and the only female of the group. She is nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Glutton'''"|大喰らい|Ō-Gurai|{{lit.}} "Big Eater"}} because of her gigantic appetite which, however, does not affect her sinuous figure.{{gnr|ch|498}} She has eaten the Age-Age Fruit, which allows her to change her own age (which she uses to disguise herself) as well as others, making her opponents either too young or too old to fight her; despite her appearance, she is a 12-year-old child. She is the captain of the Bonney Pirates, mostly consisting of fishermen acquainted with her.{{gnr|ch|499}} Born to Revolutionary [[List of One Piece characters#Ginny|Ginny]] and a World Noble, she was raised by [[Bartholomew Kuma]] from childhood, making her princess of the [[List of One Piece characters#Sorbet Kingdom|Sorbet Kingdom]] during Kuma's reign.{{Gnr|ch|1100}} After the Paramount War, she and her crew were defeated and captured by the [[Blackbeard Pirates]], and she was subsequently arrested by the [[Marines (One Piece)|Marine]] fleet led by [[Sakazuki (One Piece)|Sakazuki]]. Somehow, she managed to escape, showing herself wandering the streets incognito after the two year timeskip. During the World Meeting, she infiltrated Marijoa to rescue Kuma, eventually catching up to the Straw Hats at Egghead for similar matters. Jewelry Bonney is voiced by [[Reiko Kiuchi]] and later by [[Reiko Takagi]] in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, she is voiced by Laura Wetsel. The character is named after the real life pirate [[Anne Bonney]].{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/one-piece-real-life-pirates-inspired-characters/ |title=One Piece: 10 Real Pirates That Inspired The Characters' Creation |author=Caleb Greenough |date=June 14, 2022 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}} ===Kid Pirates=== ====Eustass Kid==== {{nihongo|'''Eustass''' "'''Captain'''" '''Kid'''|ユースタス・キャプテン・キッド|Yūsutasu "Kyaputen" Kiddo}} is the captain of the {{visible anchor|Kid Pirates}}, originating from the South Blue. Among his crew is his childhood friend [[#Killer|Killer]]. Kid ate the {{nihongo|Magnet-Magnet Fruit|ジキジキの実|Jiki Jiki no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to attract and control metal objects with magnetism.{{gnr|vol|99|:SBS}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-devil-fruits-function-water/ |title=10 One Piece Devil Fruits That Can Still Work In Water |author=George Voutiritsas |date=February 21, 2025 |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} He is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. During the time skip, he lost his arm after an encounter with [[Shanks (One Piece)|Shanks]], depending on a metal pieces arm created by his ability. After trying to form an alliance with [[#Scratchmen Apoo|Scratchmen Apoo]] and [[#Basil Hawkins|Basil Hawkins]], he ended up being betrayed by them and captured by [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], having to later ally himself with [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] and [[#Trafalgar Law|Law]] in their plan to defeat him. After the events at Wano, Kid's whereabouts are currently unknown after another failed attempt to assault Shanks. Eustass Kid is voiced by [[Daisuke Namikawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Justin Cook]] in the Funimation dub. Both his name and epithet are based in the real life privateer [[William "Captain" Kidd]]. ====Killer==== {{nihongo|'''Killer'''|キラー|Kirā}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Murder Machine'''"|殺戮武人|Satsuriku Bujin|{{lit}} "Massacre Soldier"}} is the combatant of the Kid Pirates and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]'s childhood friend. He usually fights using two blades, and stands out for wearing a mask on his face. After he and Kid were captured by [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], Killer was forced to eat a dud SMILE fruit, leaving him permanently smiling. In [[Wano Country|Wano]], he ended up working for Kaido's ally [[Kurozumi Orochi]] as a street assassin known as {{nihongo|Kamazo the Manslayer|人斬り鎌ぞう|Hito Kiri Kamazō}}. To get revenge on Kaido, he and the Kid Pirates ended up joining [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] and [[World Government (One Piece)#Trafalgar Law|Law]]'s alliance. Killer is voiced by [[Kenji Hamada]] in the original Japanese version and by Leo Fabian in the Funimation dub. ===Scratchmen Apoo=== {{nihongo|'''Scratchmen Apoo'''|スクラッチメン・アプー|Sukuratchimen Apū}}, also known as {{nihongo|"'''Roar of the Sea'''"|海鳴り|Umi Nari}}, is the captain of the {{nihongo|On-Air Pirates|オンエア海賊団|On Ea Kaizokudan}}, and a member of the longarm tribe. He has the power of the {{nihongo|Tone-Tone Fruit|オトオトの実|Oto Oto no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that gives him the ability to transform parts of his body into various instruments and generate music and great vibrations with them, however, sound does not affect people if they do not hear it. After the two year timeskip, he tried to form an alliance with [[#Basil Hawkins|Basil Hawkins]] and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]. However, he was affiliated with [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] to ambush them with Apoo being actually a subordinate of the [[Animal Kingdom Pirates]] as their informant, ending up with Hawkins joining Kaido and Apoo, and Kid being captured. Scratchmen Apoo is voiced by [[Mitsuaki Madono]] in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, he is voiced by Brad Venable in episodes 392-629 and ''One Piece: Stampede'' and by Brent Mukai starting in Episode 736. The character is named after the real life pirate [[Chui A-poo]]. ===Trafalgar Law=== The {{nihongo|"'''Surgeon of Death'''"|死の外科医|Shi no Gekai}}, {{nihongo|'''Trafalgar D. Water Law'''|トラファルガー・D・ワーテル・ロー|Torafarugā Dī Wāteru Rō}}, originates from the North Blue.{{gnr|ch|498|, |508|, |578|, |763}} Having eaten the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Op-Op Fruit|オペオペの実|Ope Ope no Mi}}, Law can, after generating a blue spherical area around himself, cut and teleport objects as well as perform [[body swap]]s within said blue area.{{gnr|ch|661}} He is the captain of the Heart Pirates. Originally from the White Town, Flevance, he escaped with White Lead Disease and became a member of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]]. There he met Donquixote Rosinante, the brother of Doflamingo, and together they went on an adventure to find a cure for Law. Ultimately they found the Devil Fruit, but before they escaped, Rosinante was killed by Doflamingo, leaving Law to seek out revenge. Law makes a name for himself and following the Paramount War, Law joins the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|659|, |673}} Though he enters into an alliance with Luffy and the Straw Hats to take down [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], one of the Four Emperors, Law is actually hunting down [[#Donquixote Doflamingo|Donquixote Doflamingo]].{{cite web |url=https://mein-mmo.de/en/the-5-most-loyal-allies-of-luffy-in-one-piece-who-are-not-crew-members,1242875/ |title=The 5 most loyal allies of Luffy in One Piece who are not crew members - Trafalgar Law |author=Esmeralda Eickemeyer |date=March 31, 2025 |website=mein-mmo.de}} Law's whereabouts are unknown after a devastating defeat against the Blackbeard Pirates, though he survived due to crew member and polar bear Bepo's interference. Trafalgar Law is voiced by [[Hiroshi Kamiya]] in the original Japanese version{{cite video |year=2011 |title=One Piece: 11thシーズン シャボンディ諸島篇: Piece.04 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} and by [[Matthew Mercer]] in the Funimation dub. The character's name takes inspiration after the real life pirate [[Edward Low]], as well as from the historical battles of [[Battle of Trafalgar|Trafalgar]] and [[Battle of Waterloo|Waterloo]]. ====Heart Pirates==== The {{nihongo|'''Heart Pirates'''|ハートの海賊団|Hāto no Kaizokudan}} is the pirate crew led by Trafalgar Law, consisting of twenty-one members, including: * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Bepo}}'''|ベポ}}: A [[polar bear]]-type [[Mink Tribe|mink]] and crew navigator. Bepo is voiced by [[Yasuhiro Takato]] in the original Japanese version and by Cris George in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Shachi}}'''|シャチ}}: An average-size lean man who wears an orca-shaped hat. Shachi is voiced by Takahiro Fujimoto in the original Japanese version and by Ben Bryant in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Penguin}}'''|ペンギン|Pengin}}: An average-size lean man who wears a hat with his name on it. Penguin is voiced by Keiji Hirai in the original Japanese version and by Seth Magill in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Jean Bart}}'''|ジャンバール|Janbāru}}: A large man who was a former slave of Saint Rosward. Jean Bart is voiced by [[Yasunori Masutani]] in the original Japanese version and by John McCalmont in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life privateer [[Jean Bart]]. ===Urouge=== {{nihongo|'''Urouge'''|ウルージ|Urūji}}, nicknamed the {{nihongo|"'''Mad Monk'''"|怪僧|Kaisō}}, is the high priest of the Mad Monk Pirates.{{gnr|ch|498}} He is originally from some Sky Island. Urouge ate an unidentified Devil Fruit that allows him to increase his muscle mass, expanding his muscles and enlarged body size.{{gnr|ch|508}} Urougue is voiced by Taiten Kusunoki in the original Japanese version and by Major Attaway in the Funimation dub. ===X. Drake=== {{main|World Government (One Piece)#X. Drake|l1=World Government (''One Piece'') § X. Drake}} ==Roger Pirates== The {{nihongo|'''Roger Pirates'''|ロジャー海賊団|Rojā Kaizokudan}} were the pirate crew of the late King of the Pirates, [[#Gol D. Roger|Gol D. Roger]], and were the only known crew to ever reach Laugh Tale. [[Shanks (One Piece)|Shanks]] and [[Buggy the Clown|Buggy]] started out as cabin boys on the crew. Because the Samurai [[Kozuki Oden]] could read the Poneglyphs, he, alongside his wife [[Kozuki Toki|Toki]], children [[Kozuki Momonosuke|Momonosuke]] and [[Kozuki Hiyori|Hiyori]], as well as his retainers [[Dogstorm and Cat Viper]], accompanied Roger and his crew for one year to learn the secrets of the world (such as the Void Century, ancient weapons, and the D. Family), as well as reaching the last island Laugh Tale. [[Douglas Bullet]] was an anime-exclusive former member of the Roger Pirates. The Roger Pirates disbanded prior to Roger's execution, with the current whereabouts of most of its members being unknown. ===Gol D. Roger=== {{nihongo|'''Gol D. Roger'''|ゴール・D・ロジャー|Gōru Dī Rojā}}, after gaining worldwide infamy as captain of the [[#Roger Pirates|Roger Pirates]], becomes better known as {{nihongo|'''Gold Roger'''|ゴールド・ロジャー|Gōrudo Rojā}}, the {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|King of the Pirates}}'''|海賊王|Kaizoku-Ō|{{lit}} "Pirate King"}}.{{gnr|ch|1|, |154|, |506}} Suffering from a terminal disease, he takes his crew on a complete voyage through the Grand Line before disbanding it and turning himself in to the [[World Government (One Piece)|World Government]], which claims to have captured him, while secretly entrusting his son, [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]], to [[Monkey D. Garp]].{{gnr|ch|506}} At his execution, before [[Portgas D. Rouge|Rouge]] gives birth to Ace, and 22 years before the formation of the [[Straw Hats|Straw Hat Crew]], Roger inspires the "Great Pirate Era" by announcing that his treasure, the "One Piece", is up for the taking, though they will have to find it first.{{gnr|ch|1|, |506|, |550}} It is said after Roger's death that only [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Edward Newgate|Whitebeard]] could match him in a fight and that he had the ability to hear "the voice of all things", which allowed him and his crew to learn the secret history of the world.{{gnr|ch|233|, |507}} He was also the original owner of Luffy's Straw Hat which fell into the possession of Shanks after his captain's death, with Shanks eventually passing it on to Luffy. Gol D. Roger has the highest known bounty in the series, with [[File:Berry (One Piece).svg|12px]]5,564,800,000.{{cite book|last=Oda|first=Eiichiro|title=Oden's Adventure|series=One Piece|volume=95|year=2019|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|isbn=978-1974718139|chapter=957 Ultimate}} Roger was a highly capable swordsman, skilled in advanced use of all three types of Haki.{{gnr|ch|966}} Roger is originally voiced by [[Chikao Ōtsuka]], and later by [[Masane Tsukayama]].{{cite video |title=One Piece Log Collection: East Blue |medium=DVD |language=ja |publisher=Avex Mode |year=2010}} A younger Roger is voiced by [[Takeshi Kusao]]. In the 4Kids adaptation, Roger is voiced by Frederick B. Owens.{{cite video |title=One Piece: Volume 1: King of the Pirates |medium=DVD |publisher=Viz Media |year=2006 |isbn=978-1-59861-000-0}} [[Eric Stuart]] initially voiced Roger before being replaced with Owens. In the Funimation English adaptation, he is voiced by Sean Hennigan.{{cite video |title=One Piece: Collection 1 |medium=DVD |publisher=Funimation Entertainment |year=2011 |isbn=978-1-4210-2341-0}} In the live-action series, he is portrayed by [[Michael Dorman]]. Roger is partially based on the real life pirate [[Olivier Levasseur]]. ===Silvers Rayleigh=== {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Silvers Rayleigh}}'''|シルバーズ・レイリー|Shirubāzu Reirī}} is a swordsman and the first mate of the Roger Pirates. Having encountered a young Roger in his youth, he joined the crew as his first mate, developing his swordsmanship to the point he is known as the {{nihongo|{{visible anchor|"'''Dark King'''"}}|冥王|Mei-Ō}} and considered to be Roger's right-hand man.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|603}} After Roger's death, Rayleigh retires on the [[Sabaody Archipelago]] as a ship coater and gambler.{{gnr|ch|500}} He encounters and reveals his identity to the Straw Hat Crew on their arrival, coating the ship and becoming a vital ally for the crew. Following the war between the [[Whitebeard Pirates]] and the [[World Government (One Piece)|World Government]], he trains [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] to use Haki for two years.{{gnr|ch|503}}{{cite web |url=https://mein-mmo.de/en/the-5-most-loyal-allies-of-luffy-in-one-piece-who-are-not-crew-members,1242875/2/ |title=The 5 most loyal allies of Luffy in One Piece who are not crew members - Silvers Rayleigh |author=Esmeralda Eickemeyer |date=March 31, 2025 |website=mein-mmo.de}} He is one of the only men to be respected by the Kuja Tribe, having married their former empress [[World Government (One Piece)#Shakuyaku|Shakuyaku]]. Silvers Rayleigh is voiced by [[Keiichi Sonobe]] in the original Japanese version and by Bruce Carey in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life statesman and explorer [[Walter Raleigh]]. ===Scopper Gaban=== {{nihongo|'''Scopper Gaban'''|スコッパー・ギャバン|Sukoppā Gyaban}} was the navigator of the Roger Pirates. He is known for his proficient skill in wielding axes and amorous nature, later being nicknamed the "Left Hand of the Pirate King". During his time in the Roger Pirates, he was infamous for his constant one-night stands which he is ashamed of after being acquainted with Ripley. After Roger's death, he retired in Elbaph and fathered the half-giant Collun through the giant [[List of One Piece characters#Ripley|Ripley]].{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1139|,|1147}} During the fight against [[Imu (One Piece)|Imu]], Scopper Gaban loses his left arm. Scopper Gaban is voiced by [[Toshiyuki Morikawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Ian Sinclair (voice actor)|Ian Sinclair]] in the Funimation dub. === Crocus === {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Crocus}}'''|クロッカス|Kurokkasu}} was the doctor of the Roger Pirates, who joined late to help with Roger's. He is the sole human resident of the Twin Capes, and who takes care of the giant whale [[Laboon (One Piece)|Laboon]]. Crocus was voiced by [[Gorō Naya]] and [[Masuo Amada]] in the original Japanese version, and by Jerry Russell, Burl W. Proctor and Gregory Lush in the Funimation dub. In the live-action series, Crocus is portrayed by [[Clive Russell]].{{cite web |date=June 26, 2024 |title='One Piece' Adds Trio of Actors to Season 2 (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/one-piece-season-2-giant-warrior-pirates-crocus-1235932383/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}} ===Other Roger Pirates=== * {{nihongo|'''Donquino'''|ドンキーノ|Donkīno}}: A large man who is the helmsman of the Rogers Pirates. Donquino is voiced by Yūsuke Shirooka in the original Japanese version and by Van Barr Jr. in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Moon Isaac Jr.'''|ムーン・アイザックJr.|Mūn Aizakku Junia}} : A long-nosed rotund man who is the tactical officer of the Rogers Pirates. Moon Isaac Jr. is voiced by Yūsuke Shirooka in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Millet Pine'''|ミレ・パイン|Mire Pain}}: A short rotund man who is the interrogator/torturer of the Roger Pirates and wears a horned helmet. * {{nihongo|'''Rowing'''|ローウィング|Rowingu}}: A short rotund man who is the [[scholar]] of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Erio'''|エリオ}}: A slim man ina white fedora who is the [[Data broker|information broker]] of the Roger Pirates. Following the disbandment of the Rogers Pirates, Erio's whereabouts are unknown. Erio is voiced by Tom Henry in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Spencer'''|スペンサー|Supensā}}: The [[intelligence officer]] of the Roger Pirates. Spencer is voiced by Kristian Eros in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Petermoo'''|ピータームー|Pītāmū}}: A short man with an egg-shaped body who is the [[Gunner (rank)|gunner]] of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Blumarine'''|ブルマリン|Burumarin}}: A short older man who is the shipwright of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''MAX Marx'''|MAX マークス|Makkusu Mākusu}}: A tall muscular man who is the cook of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Seagull Guns Nozdon'''|シーガル・ガンズ・ノズドン|Shīgaru Ganzu Nozudon}}: A very tall and muscular man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. Seagull Guns Nozdon is voiced by Neiji Hirai in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Mr. Momora'''|Mr. モモラ|Misutā Momora}}: A very tall and thin man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. Mr. Momora is voiced by Ryōhei Arai in the original Japanese version and by Josh Putnam in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Jacksonbanner'''|ジャクソンバナー|Jakusonbanā}}: A tall slim man who is the musician of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Sunbell'''|サンベル|Sanberu}}: A fish-man of indeterminate species and a member of the Roger Pirates. Taro is voiced by Toshiya Chiba in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Doringo'''|ドリンゴ}}: A shorter man with long limbs and member of the Roger Pirates whose jacket has bat-like wings on its back. Doringo is voiced by Yukinori Okuhata in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Ganryu'''|眼竜|Ganryū}}: A tall muscular man and a member of the Roger Pirates. Ganryu is voiced by Kazumasa Fukagawa in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''CB Gallant'''|CBギャラン|Shībī Gyaran}}: A large and very muscular man with short legs who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Yui'''|ユーイ|Yūi}}: A member of the Roger Pirates with wavy hair that goes straight up. * {{nihongo|'''Rangram'''|ラングラム|Ranguramu}}: A tall fit man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Colonel Mugren'''|ミュグレン大佐|Myuguren Taisa}}: A large man with broad shoulders who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Bankuro'''|バンクロ}}: A short slender man with a puffy hair and beard who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Yamon'''|ヤモン}}: A member of the Roger Pirates who fights with a spear. ==East Blue== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the East Blue sea. Former pirates in the East Blue include: * [[Zeff (One Piece)|"'''Red Foot'''" '''Zeff''']], now the Head Chef at Baratie. * '''[[Gaimon]]''' was a pirate until his body became trapped in a chest. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Koze}}'''|コゼ}} and {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Packy}}'''|パッキー|Pakkī}} were two members of the Yes Pirates. Koze is tall and thin while Packy is bulky and muscular. They were captured by [[Smoker (One Piece)|Smoker]] and [[Tashigi]] in Loguetown and arrested.{{gnr|ch|96}} * The [[#Usopp Pirates|Usopp Pirates]] (see below) * The [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]] were also stationed in this sea for several years until they were arrested. ===Black Cat Pirates=== The '''Black Cat Pirates''' are a cat-themed crew of pirates led by their captain [[#Kuro|Kuro]] who considers them as nothing but pawns to carry out his plans and, if he so pleases, to die for him.{{gnr|ch|38}} ====Kuro==== {{nihongo|'''Kuro'''|クロ|{{lit}} "Black"}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"Kuro of the Thousand Plans"|百計のクロ|Hyakkei no Kuro}}, is the captain of the [[#Black Cat Pirates|Black Cat Pirates]], who is known for his elaborate schemes.{{gnr|ch|26}} Wishing to leave his identity behind, and to escape the wearying pirate lifestyle of always being on the run,{{gnr|ch|37}} he uses the name '''Klahadore''' (クラハドール ''Kurahadōru'') and becomes butler to [[Kaya (One Piece)|Kaya]], a friend of [[Usopp]].{{gnr|ch|23}} He considers his crew as nothing but pawns to carry out his plans and, if he so pleases, to die for him.{{gnr|ch|38}} Kuro fights using a pair of gloves equipped with long, straight, single edged blades. Wearing these, he adopted his signature habit of adjusting his constantly slipping glasses by using only the palm of his hand to avoid cutting his face.{{gnr|ch|33}} In the anime, Kuro resumes pirate life following his defeat and sees that the bounty for Luffy has gone up following Arlong's defeat.{{cite episode |series=One Piece |series-link=One Piece (1999 TV series) |title=Bounty! Straw Hat Luffy Becomes Known to the World! |episode-link=One Piece season 1#ep45 |season=1 |number=45 |date=October 25, 2000 |network=[[Fuji Television]]}} In the Japanese anime television series, Kuro is voiced by [[Kōichi Hashimoto]]. In the 4Kids English adaptation, he is voiced by [[Gary Mack]] while his voice actor in the Funimation English adaptation is [[Kent Williams (voice actor)|Kent Williams]]. In the [[One Piece (2023 TV series)|live-action series]], he is portrayed by Alexandar Maniatis.{{cite web |last1=Del Rosario |first1=Alexandra |date=June 6, 2022 |title=Netflix 'One Piece' Live-Action Series Adds Six To Cast; Star Iñaki Godoy & Showrunners Tease Epic Sets |url=https://deadline.com/2022/06/netflix-one-piece-live-action-series-adds-six-to-cast-star-inaki-godoy-showrunners-tease-epic-sets-1235038196/ |access-date=June 6, 2022 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=June 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220606165856/https://deadline.com/2022/06/netflix-one-piece-live-action-series-adds-six-to-cast-star-inaki-godoy-showrunners-tease-epic-sets-1235038196/ |url-status=live}} Carl Kimlinger of ''[[Anime News Network]]'' praised Kuro as being "both unspeakably cool and utterly vile".{{cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/one-piece/dvd-season-1|title=Review: One Piece: DVD—Season 1 Part 1 Uncut|publisher=Anime News Network|date=June 3, 2008|last=Kimlinger|first=Carl|access-date=December 6, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111118230607/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/one-piece/dvd-season-1|archive-date=November 18, 2011|url-status=live}} ====Django==== {{main|World Government (One Piece)#Django|l1=World Government (''One Piece'') § Django}} '''Django''' is the former captain and previously first mate of the Black Cat Pirates. He later joins the Marines. ===={{visible anchor|Siam|Sham}} and {{visible anchor|Butchie}}==== {{nihongo|'''Siam'''|シャム|Shamu}} and {{nihongo|'''Butchie'''|ブチ|Buchi}}, known as the {{nihongo|'''Nyaban Brothers'''|ニャーバン・{{Ruby-ja|兄弟|ブラザーズ}}|Nyāban Burazāzu}}, are the protector guards of the Bezan Black, the crew's ship.{{gnr|ch|31}} Both of them face Zoro, being defeated by him. |url=https://collider.com/one-piece-netflix-live-action-series-cast-plot-sneak-peek-episode-details/ |title=Netflix's 'One Piece' Live-Action Series: Cast, Plot, Sneak Peek, and Everything We Know So
